topics.label: Introduction to cancer causation and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic factors, environmental exposure, and cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how clonal evolution, endogenous mutational processes, inherited genetics, and environmental epidemiology contribute to the overall balance of cancer risk.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogenic agents, tumour initiation, and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which biological, physical, and chemical agents act as initiators or promoters to induce malignancy across different tissues and developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating mutagenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques used to establish whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit assessment
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture by summarising the main concepts of environmental cancer risk and considering how individuals and society weigh carcinogenic hazards against practical benefits.
